items.title: 基因序列預測模型AlphaGenome 2深入細胞層次，追查疾病相關DNA變異
items.summary: DeepMind發布基因序列預測模型AlphaGenome 2，能依不同細胞類型與狀態，預測DNA變異對基因表現的影響。前代模型主要分析組織整體的分子活動，新版則能辨識只在特定細胞中發揮作用的變異，協助研究人員追查疾病相關的基因調控機制。

items.title: fix(update): updating from 2026.11.3 fails when Workboard is installe…
items.summary: fix(update): updating from 2026.11.3 fails when Workboard is installed (#197526) * fix(update): answer released drivers in the schema shape they verify Published 2026.11.3 drivers read schema rows from the candidate worker but compare every non-shared row against the agent schema, so Workboard's own user_version 0 failed the second Doctor ("expected schema 41, found 0") and blocked rollback. Those drivers omit includeLocalStoreVersions; their replies now carry only shared and agent-owned rows (owners, registered paths, agent directory overrides), the same set the 2026.11.3 worker itself publishes. Discovery, capture, backup and generation checks still include Workboard. The candidate worker also applies the existing 2026.11.1 Workboard-only PostgreSQL normalization to the config released drivers serialize, so the snapshot no longer refuses with "Existing SQLite state data cannot switch engines". Refs #197320 * fix(update): read 2026.11.3 rehearsal configs as SQLite Rehearsal state is private SQLite images, never live PostgreSQL anchors. Current drivers write that projection into the rehearsal config; 2026.11.3 copies the source database selection unchanged, so the candidate doctor treated the copied shared state as PostgreSQL and refused it with "Existing SQLite state data cannot switch engines". The candidate's config read now applies the same projection when the update rehearsal contract is present. The PostgreSQL regression continues past the snapshot into the candidate doctor's database preflight with the config a 2026.11.3 driver writes. Refs #197320

items.title: feat(identity): accept co-author credit from trusted-proxy headers (#…
items.summary: feat(identity): accept co-author credit from trusted-proxy headers (#196867) * feat: let profiles configure Git co-author details Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant * fix: preserve co-author consent across profile changes Reset consent when the first supplied address arrives, preserve the selected address and its consent through merges, and keep optional organization defaults from exhausting user preference capacity. Transfer custom details before consent when merge capacity is limited. Keep optional co-author constants outside browser startup. Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant * fix(identity): address co-author review and CI integration Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant * refactor(identity): limit co-author details to trusted proxy claims Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant * fix(identity): preserve proxy credit consent and profile presentation Bind organization credit to the observed details and current proxy policy, refresh Profile safely, preserve verified GitHub mentions, and repair CI fixtures and canonical configuration metadata. Fold in the related OIDC presentation fix: do not infer a display name from an issuer-qualified subject, hide opaque authentication aliases from Linked emails, and preserve the canonical principal bindings and profile IDs. Keep mutation responses consistent with profile reads and cover name/avatar saves in the resident and real-Gateway regressions. Show selected credit details inline beside consent, distinguish sign-in emails, and expose only the verified public-GitHub noreply pair in self-profile reads. Regenerate the owning protocol validators and align the Profile browser fixtures. Co-authored-by: sallyom * refactor(identity): simplify co-author state and coverage Keep consent local to identity reads and consolidate canonical documentation, protected metadata, admission and Profile coverage. Preserve full preference capacity, both sign-in transports, explicit organization consent and verified GitHub variants. Co-authored-by: sallyom --------- Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant Co-authored-by: sallyom
